facts.statement: The genus Seitaad was described by Sertich and Loewen in 2010.
Phylogenetic studies place Seitaad in the family Massospondylidae, though an alternative placement in Plateosauridae is considered less probable.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic study of Seitaad found it to be a plateosaur sauropodomorph, placing it in Massospondylidae or alternatively (a less probable position) in Plateosauridae

facts.statement: Seitaad is classified as a sauropodomorph dinosaur within the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: The known remains of Seitaad consist of a single articulated partial postcranial holotype skeleton designated UMNH VP 18040.
facts.quote: Seitaad is known from an articulated partial postcranial holotype skeleton referred to as UMNH VP 18040

facts.statement: Seitaad ruessi is the only known species within the extinct genus Seitaad.
facts.quote: Seitaad ruessi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Seitaad

facts.statement: Fossil evidence dates Seitaad to the Pliensbachian to Toarcian stages, between 192.9 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Toarcian (192.9 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Seitaad fossils were collected from the Navajo Sandstone near Comb Ridge in San Juan County, Utah.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Lower Jurassic Navajo Sandstone, the uppermost unit of the Glen Canyon Group, dating to the Pliensbachian stage, near Comb Ridge, San Juan County

facts.statement: Although the skull is missing, Seitaad is estimated to have reached a length of 6.5 to 7 meters.
facts.quote: Pese a que le falta la cabeza, se estima que llegó a medir entre 6,5 y 7 metros

facts.statement: The generic name Seitaad is derived from a Navajo mythological sand monster that buried its victims in dunes.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Séít'áád (Navajo language), a mythological sand monster from the Diné folklore who buried its victims in dunes

facts.statement: The species name 'ruessi' honors Everett Ruess, an artist and naturalist who disappeared in southern Utah in 1934.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Everett Ruess, a young artist, poet and naturalist, who mysteriously disappeared in 1934 while exploring southern Utah

facts.statement: Seitaad is the second basal sauropodomorph dinosaur identified in North America.
facts.quote: Seitaad is the second basal sauropodomorph dinosaur to have been identified in North America

facts.statement: The precise placement of Seitaad within the clade Plateosauria remains poorly understood.
facts.quote: but its placement within the Plateosauria is not well understood
